source_policy: SEER Cancer Stat Facts (non-Hodgkin lymphoma as the closest population denominator for B-cell lymphomas), ACS Cancer Facts & Figures 2026. Citable; refresh yearly. NCCN not used.
scope_note: B-cell lymphomas are the large majority of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL); SEER reports NHL as the population aggregate. Entity-level rates (DLBCL, FL, CLL/SLL, MCL, etc.) vary and should be stated per-entity where needed.

incidence.us_annual_new_cases: NHL ~79,320 projected for 2026 (B-cell lymphomas are the large majority)
incidence.rank_among_cancers: NHL ~3.8% of new cancer cases; DLBCL is the most common aggressive B-cell lymphoma, follicular lymphoma the most common indolent one

mortality.five_year_survival_overall: NHL ~74% aggregate; highly entity-dependent (e.g., indolent FL very high; aggressive subtypes lower but curable in a substantial fraction)
mortality.survival_by_stage: Ann Arbor stage and entity (DLBCL vs FL vs MCL) drive prognosis more than a single aggregate figure; cell-of-origin and double-hit status further stratify DLBCL
mortality.trend: Death rates falling ~2.4%/yr, reflecting rituximab-era and cellular-therapy gains

risk_factors.detail: Most NHL diagnosed at 65-74; incidence rises with age
HIV, post-transplant immunosuppression, inborn errors of immunity (drives immune deficiency/dysregulation-associated LBCL)
EBV, H. pylori (gastric MALT), HCV, HTLV-1, HHV-8 associations by entity
Sjögren, Hashimoto, celiac (MALT and other lymphomas)
First-degree family history of hematologic malignancy

modalities: no screening test (NHL is not screened in the general population)
screening.guideline_summary: There is no population screening for lymphoma; diagnosis is tissue-based (excisional biopsy preferred) prompted by symptoms or findings. NCCN not used.
screening.notes: Diagnosis depends on adequate tissue and a full IHC/molecular workup; cell-of-origin and FISH (MYC/BCL2/BCL6) are central to classification

epidemiology.presentation: Painless lymphadenopathy, B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), fatigue, or extranodal/organ-specific findings; aggressive subtypes present rapidly, indolent ones often incidentally

acs_ff_2026.authors: Siegel RL, Kratzer TB, Wagle NS, Sung H, Jemal A.
acs_ff_2026.title: Cancer statistics, 2026

verification_status: VERIFIED against SEER Cancer Stat Facts (2026 release) and ACS Cancer Facts & Figures 2026 via live search on build date; pathologist should still confirm before publication. Stats are the fastest-aging content — refresh yearly.
